summary: Malaysia's mobility is back to near‑normal levels with the MF‑Index at 83 and public transport usage exceeding pre‑pandemic daily trips. Fuel savings remain substantial at 35.7 million litres per week, but high fuel prices and uneven WFH adoption pose emerging risks. Targeted policy tweaks can lock in the gains while mitigating sectoral exposure.

signals.detail: Weekly fuel savings of 35.7 M litres represent 42% of the MCO peak, confirming that WFH and modal shifts continue to deliver significant energy efficiency despite higher fuel prices.
Daily public‑transport trips reached 1.49 M, slightly above the pre‑pandemic average of 1.43 M, indicating a robust recovery and effective PT incentives.
High mobility scores in Logistics (92), Construction (95) and Retail (85) coincide with the highest risk ratings, exposing these sectors to fuel‑price volatility and potential productivity losses.
WFH adoption ranges from 60% in Public & GLCs to only 5% in Construction, creating unequal exposure to fuel cost shocks; equity‑focused incentives are needed for low‑adoption sectors.
Sustained PT usage and continued fuel savings suggest a gradual shift away from private car travel, which can be accelerated by further PT subsidies and congestion pricing.

recommendation: Maintain targeted fuel‑price relief for high‑risk sectors while expanding PT subsidies to keep daily ridership above 1.6 M trips by end‑2027. Introduce sector‑specific WFH incentives for Logistics, Construction and Retail to lower mobility scores below 80 and reduce fuel demand by an additional 10% weekly.
